title: Actionable SDK exceptions, retry hints, and streaming error ergonomics
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Create a unified, developer-friendly error surface across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs that provides machine-readable codes, human-actionable messages, and explicit retry/streaming guidance. This ticket covers the exception shape, retry hint semantics, streaming partial-response behavior, per-language ergonomic wrapper APIs, migration plan, and examples. Goal: reduce customer confusion, make automated retries safer, and improve observability when retries/fallbacks happen.
acceptance_criteria: Define a single canonical error schema accepted by public API and internal runtime: code, message, retryable, retry_after_seconds (optional), hint, doc_url, request_id, http_status, partial_response_marker (optional)
SDKs (Python/TS/Go) expose the canonical fields on exception objects and provide typed helpers: is_retryable(), get_retry_after(), and link_to_docs()

Streaming clients emit a deterministic event when an unrecoverable error happens mid-stream with last_partial_tokens and retry_hint; SDKs provide a composable stream wrapper to optionally resume or surface the partial result
Provide usage examples for each language showing safe automatic retry patterns and backoff recommended defaults
E2E tests that assert mapping of HTTP runtime errors to SDK exceptions and correct telemetry tags (error.code, retryable boolean, request_id)
Documentation and migration guide that lists previous error types and how they map to the new schema
design_decisions: Use stable string codes (namespace dot-free but descriptive) instead of pure integers (e.g., "rate_limited", "model_unavailable", "invalid_request"). Strings are easier to read in logs and safer across languages.
Keep retryable separate from http_status to avoid inferring retryability from 5xx alone. Explicit flag reduces accidental retries for client-side errors.
Include an optional retry_after_seconds (float) field when server can give a specific backoff window. SDK helpers convert to Duration/number types per language.

For streaming: emit an "error" event with last_partial_tokens plus an enum-style retry_hint: "NONE" | "RETRY_IMMEDIATELY" | "RETRY_AFTER" | "RESUME_UNSUPPORTED". This keeps event loop simple and language-consistent.
Expose a small compat shim so older user code still sees familiar exception classes with new properties available (e.g., Python: LegacyAPIError inherits from RedwoodSDKError and has .code/.retryable)
Telemetry: mandate three tags: error.code, error.retryable, request_id. This prevents siloed interpretation of codes across services.
implementation_plan: Schema: add canonical JSON schema to runtime -> runtime returns new error envelope in all deployments (hosted/dedicated/private)
Runtime change: map existing error mapping to canonical fields and ensure runtime always sets request_id and http_status
SDK changes: implement language-specific exception classes with helper methods. Avoid breaking changes by providing compatibility aliases
Streaming client changes: standardize stream event names and semantics; implement last_partial_tokens serialization and resume hint handling
Docs & examples: draft migration guide, developer-focused quickstart, and safe retry recipes for common scenarios
Testing: unit tests per SDK, integration tests against staging runtime, and chaos tests to validate backoff + partial response handling
Rollout: feature-flag runtime behavior; SDKs opt-in to v2 error shape while runtime emits both v1 and v2 for 2 release cycles
testing_plan: Unit: verify exception attributes and helper methods across Python/TS/Go
Integration: run a test harness that injects runtime errors (rate_limit, backend_oom, network_timeout) and assert SDK mapping and retry helpers behave as expected
Streaming: simulate mid-stream disconnects, server-side error events, and ensure SDK emits error event with last_partial_tokens and correct retry_hint
Telemetry: assert that synthetic errors include tags error.code, error.retryable, request_id, and are visible in the dashboard
Canary: roll SDK minor versions to internal tenants and observe error handling patterns and customer support tickets for 2 weeks
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (runtime): implement v2 error envelope behind feature flag and start emitting for 10% of internal requests
Phase 2 (SDKs): release non-breaking minor SDKs with new exceptions and helpers; include opt-in example: Client(enable_new_errors=True)
Phase 3 (docs + migration): publish migration guide + CLI lint tool to detect old error usage in codebases
Phase 4 (full switch): after 2 release cycles and no high-severity issues, enable v2 error envelope by default and deprecate v1 mapping with 90-day notice
